title: Reimagine Robotics Exits Stealth with Robots That Learn on the Job
summary: Reimagine Robotics came out of stealth on August 3, 2026 with pre-seed funding from Fly Ventures, firstminute capital and angel investors. Founded in April 2025 with offices in London and Sydney, it is led by CEO Jonathan Scholz, who founded Google DeepMind's Applied Robotics team in London and ran it for seven years, alongside former DeepMind colleagues Oleg Sushkov, Akhil Raju and Misha Denil. The pitch is teaching by demonstration and correction rather than programming — show the robot a task, correct it when it errs — which the company says cuts the time to prototype a new robot behaviour from roughly a day to about 10 minutes. Early applications are advanced manufacturing and electronics disassembly, including 3D-printer tending (removing beds, working latches, pressing controls) and taking apart hard drives for material recovery.
whyItMatters: The bottleneck in factory robotics is not capability but the engineer-weeks each new task costs, which is why short-run and mixed-line work stays manual. Compressing behaviour authoring from a day to ten minutes, done by the person who already knows the job rather than a robotics integrator, is what would make automation economical below high-volume scale. That the founding team built DeepMind's applied robotics group is the credibility here: this is lab manipulation research being pointed at the un-automated middle of manufacturing.
